changes.from: a future-inextendible causal geodesic gamma: [0,T) -> M with T < infinity in affine parameter is visible from I+ iff there exists q in I+ AND t0 in [0,T) such that the TAIL gamma([t0,T)) is contained in J^-(q) intersect M. Visibility is a property of the singular END of the geodesic, so the tail formulation is used; for causal geodesics the tail and whole-curve readings are EQUIVALENT (past-closedness of J^-(q)), so no geodesic is misclassified by either reading. [rev13: the rev12 misclassification example was a non-sequitur and is removed; the predicate is unchanged - W076-GFORM-STRICTNESS-RECONCILE-06 T1, worker-040 W040-F1-STRICTNESS-ADJ-04]
changes.to: a future-inextendible causal geodesic gamma: [0,T) -> M with T < infinity in affine parameter is visible-from-I-plus-in-the-set-sense iff gamma([0,T)) is contained in the union of J^-(q) over q in I+ (intersected with M). This is the SET-based reading of the F0 taxonomy: it is implied by the single-q tail predicate and is therefore strictly weaker than it (T2: tail => set, 0 violations; T3/T4: the readings coincide when I+ is finite or gamma has a causal maximum and are separated by the omega-chain otherwise). changes.from: there is NO visible_singularity_from_I_plus: for every future-inextendible causal geodesic gamma of finite affine length, for every q in I+ and every t0 in [0,T), the tail gamma([t0,T)) is NOT contained in J^-(q) intersect M - no single point of I+ causally precedes the singular end of gamma. This is NOT equivalent to 'gamma is contained in B = M minus J^-(I+)': B-containment is strictly stronger, and a geodesic may begin in J^-(I+) and end in the black-hole region. [R1 F02 accepted; the earlier 'i.e. inside B' equivalence was false]
